191:     # ---- NIC placement --------------------------------------------------
192:     # vrnetlab enumerates NICs by PCI slot. To get a clean
193:     # container-ethN -> vAOS-1/1/N mapping with EMP as the management port, we
194:     # force every NIC onto bridge pci.1 with explicit, ordered slots and
195:     # reserve the slot at MGMT_NIC_INDEX for the management NIC (= EMP).
196: 
197:     @staticmethod
198:     def _eth_to_nic_index(eth_i):
199:         """container eth index -> guest NIC index (skipping the EMP/mgmt slot)."""
200:         return eth_i - 1 if eth_i - 1 < MGMT_NIC_INDEX else eth_i
201: 
202:     @staticmethod
203:     def _set_slot(dev_str, nic_index):
204:         """Force a -device string onto pci.1 at slot (nic_index + 1)."""
205:         dev_str = re.sub(r",bus=pci\.\d+", "", dev_str)
206:         dev_str = re.sub(r",addr=0x[0-9a-fA-F]+", "", dev_str)
207:         return dev_str + ",bus=pci.1,addr=0x%x" % (nic_index + 1)
208: 
209:     def gen_mgmt(self):
210:         # Put the management NIC on the EMP slot (guest index 2).
211:         res = super().gen_mgmt()
212:         for i, tok in enumerate(res):
213:             if tok == "-device":
214:                 res[i + 1] = self._set_slot(res[i + 1], MGMT_NIC_INDEX)
215:         return res
216: 
217:     def gen_nics(self):
218:         # Re-slot each data NIC so container ethN lands on its target guest index.
219:         res = super().gen_nics()
220:         # vrnetlab skips NICs above the highest wired ethN, and the guest numbers
221:         # NICs in enumeration order. If eth1/eth2 are not wired, the management
222:         # NIC shifts down and is no longer EMP. Always add unconnected dummies.
223:         present = set(int(n) for n in re.findall(r"netdev=p(\d+)", " ".join(res)))
224:         for eth_i in range(1, MGMT_NIC_INDEX + 1):
225:             if eth_i not in present:
226:                 res.extend([
227:                     "-device", "%s,netdev=p%02d" % (self.nic_type, eth_i),
228:                     "-netdev", "socket,id=p%02d,listen=:%d" % (eth_i, 10000 + eth_i),
229:                 ])
230:         for i, tok in enumerate(res):
231:             if tok == "-device":
232:                 m = re.search(r"netdev=p(\d+)", res[i + 1])
233:                 if m:
234:                     eth_i = int(m.group(1))
235:                     res[i + 1] = self._set_slot(res[i + 1], self._eth_to_nic_index(eth_i))
236:         return res
237: 
238:     def _log_port_map(self):
239:         """Log the container-interface <-> vAOS-port mapping for the operator."""
240:         self.logger.info("vAOS NIC mapping (EMP = vrnetlab management):")
241:         for nic in sorted(self.port_map):
242:             port = self.port_map[nic]
243:             if nic == MGMT_NIC_INDEX:
244:                 src = "vrnetlab management (NAT, or container eth0 in mgmt-passthrough)"
245:             else:
246:                 eth = nic + 1 if nic < MGMT_NIC_INDEX else nic
247:                 src = "container eth%d" % eth
248:             self.logger.info("  guest NIC%-2d  vAOS %-8s  <-  %s", nic, port, src)
249:         self.logger.info("  => eth1=1/1/1, eth2=1/1/2, eth3=1/1/3 ... EMP = management")
250: 
251:     def bootstrap_spin(self):
252:         """Poll the serial console until the OmniSwitch login prompt appears."""
253:         if self.spins > 6000:
254:             self.logger.warning("Too many spins, restarting VM")
255:             self.stop()
256:             self.start()
257:             return
258: 
259:         (ridx, match, res) = self.tn.expect([b"login:"], 1)
260:         # keep the boot output, in case the link-up line shows before login:
261:         self._boot_out = getattr(self, "_boot_out", b"") + res
262:         if match and ridx == 0:
263:             self.logger.info("vAOS reached login prompt")
264:             if os.environ.get("VAOS_BOOTSTRAP", "true").lower() != "false":
265:                 try:
266:                     self.bootstrap_config()
267:                 except Exception as e:
268:                     self.logger.error("vAOS bootstrap failed: %s", e)
269:             self.running = True
270:             self.tn.close()
271:             return
272: 
273:         if res != b"":
274:             self.logger.trace("OUTPUT: %s" % res.decode(errors="ignore"))
275:             self.spins = 0
276: 
277:         self.spins += 1
278:         return
279: 
280:     # ---- containerlab save ----------------------------------------------
281: 
282:     def work(self):
283:         super().work()
284:         if self.running and os.path.exists(SAVE_REQUEST):
285:             self.save_config()
286: 
287:     def save_config(self):
288:         """Save the configuration and store a snapshot for containerlab save."""
289:         self.logger.info("containerlab save requested")
290:         try:
291:             os.remove(SAVE_REQUEST)
292:         except OSError:
293:             pass
294:         result = "ok"
295:         try:
296:             self.tn.open()
297:             self.tn.write(b"\r")
298:             ridx, _, _ = self.tn.expect([PROMPT_RE, b"login:"], 15)
299:             if ridx == 1:
300:                 username = os.environ.get("VAOS_USERNAME") or self.username
301:                 password = os.environ.get("VAOS_PASSWORD") or self.password
302:                 if not self._login(username, password):
303:                     raise RuntimeError("could not log in on the console")
304:             elif ridx != 0:
305:                 raise RuntimeError("no prompt on the console (is a console session open?)")
306:             self._send("write memory flash-synchro", timeout=180)
307:             buf = self._send("show configuration snapshot", timeout=120)
308:             config = self._extract_snapshot(buf)
309:             if not config.strip():
310:                 raise RuntimeError("empty configuration snapshot")
311:             with open(SAVED_CONFIG, "w") as f:
312:                 f.write(config)
313:             self.logger.info("configuration saved to %s", SAVED_CONFIG)
314:             self.tn.write(b"exit\r")
315:         except Exception as e:
316:             result = "error: %s" % e
317:             self.logger.error("containerlab save failed: %s", e)
318:         finally:
319:             try:
320:                 self.tn.close()
321:             except Exception:
322:                 pass
323:             with open(SAVE_DONE, "w") as f:
324:                 f.write(result + "\n")
325: 
326:     @staticmethod
327:     def _extract_snapshot(buf):
328:         """Keep the configuration lines of "show configuration snapshot".
329: 
330:         Async console messages ("+++ Link 1/1/4 operationally up") can be
331:         printed in the middle of a line: "spb+++ Link ...\n isis ..." is
332:         rejoined as "spb isis ...".
333:         """
334:         lines = buf.decode(errors="ignore").replace("\r", "").split("\n")
335:         for i, line in enumerate(lines):
336:             if "show configuration snapshot" in line:
337:                 lines = lines[i + 1:]
338:                 break
339:         out = []
340:         i = 0
341:         while i < len(lines):
342:             line = lines[i]
343:             i += 1
344:             if LINE_PROMPT_RE.match(line):
345:                 break  # CLI prompt after the output
346:             if line.startswith("+++") or ASYNC_HEADER_RE.match(line):
347:                 continue  # async console message on its own line
348:             pos = line.find("+++")
349:             if pos > 0:
350:                 # message inserted mid-line: the rest of the line follows it
351:                 while i < len(lines) and lines[i].startswith("+++"):
352:                     i += 1
353:                 rest = lines[i] if i < len(lines) else ""
354:                 i += 1
355:                 line = line[:pos] + rest
356:             out.append(line)
357:         while out and not out[-1].strip():
358:             out.pop()
359:         while out and not out[0].strip():
360:             out.pop(0)
361:         return "\n".join(out) + "\n"
362: 
363:     # ---- console bootstrap ---------------------------------------------
364: 
365:     def _send(self, cmd, timeout=30):
366:         """Send one CLI command and wait for the "->" prompt. If vAOS says it
367:         is not ready yet, wait and send the command again."""
368:         deadline = time.time() + READY_TIMEOUT
369:         while True:
370:             self.logger.info("vAOS> %s", cmd)
371:             self.tn.write((cmd + "\r").encode())
372:             ridx, _, buf = self.tn.expect([PROMPT_RE], timeout)
373:             if ridx != 0:
374:                 self.logger.warning("no prompt after '%s' (continuing)", cmd)
375:                 return buf
376:             if not re.search(NOT_READY_RE, buf):
377:                 return buf
378:             if time.time() > deadline:
379:                 self.logger.error("vAOS still not ready after %ds, giving up on '%s'",
380:                                   READY_TIMEOUT, cmd)
381:                 return buf
382:             self.logger.info("vAOS not ready yet, retrying in %ds", READY_RETRY_DELAY)
383:             time.sleep(READY_RETRY_DELAY)
384: 
385:     def _sync_emp_mac(self, emp):
386:         """mgmt passthrough: copy the EMP MAC address to the container eth0.
387: 
388:         vrnetlab gives the container eth0 the MAC of the VM management NIC, so
389:         that traffic for the ports kept in the container (5000-5007, serial
390:         console) is accepted by the container. vAOS does not use that MAC for
391:         EMP but its own, so the launcher learns it with an ARP probe sent to
392:         the VM on tap0 and sets it on eth0.
393:         """
394:         ip = socket.inet_aton(emp.split("/")[0])
395:         try:
396:             with open("/sys/class/net/%s/address" % self.mgmt_intf) as f:
397:                 src = bytes.fromhex(f.read().strip().replace(":", ""))
398:             # ETH_P_ALL: frames from the VM are redirected to eth0 by tc on tap0
399:             # ingress; only an ETH_P_ALL socket sees them before that
400:             sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_PACKET, socket.SOCK_RAW, socket.htons(0x0003))
401:             sock.bind(("tap0", 0))
402:             sock.settimeout(1)
403:         except OSError as e:
404:             self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync skipped: %s", e)
405:             return
406:         # ARP probe: who-has <EMP IP>, sender IP 0.0.0.0
407:         probe = (b"\xff" * 6 + src + b"\x08\x06"
408:                  + struct.pack("!HHBBH", 1, 0x0800, 6, 4, 1)
409:                  + src + b"\x00" * 4 + b"\x00" * 6 + ip)
410:         mac = None
411:         deadline = time.time() + 30
412:         try:
413:             while mac is None and time.time() < deadline:
414:                 sock.send(probe)
415:                 end = time.time() + 2
416:                 while time.time() < end:
417:                     try:
418:                         pkt = sock.recv(2048)
419:                     except socket.timeout:
420:                         break
421:                     # ARP (reply, or gratuitous ARP) sent by the VM from the EMP IP
422:                     if len(pkt) >= 42 and pkt[12:14] == b"\x08\x06" \
423:                             and pkt[28:32] == ip and pkt[22:28] != src:
424:                         mac = pkt[22:28]
425:                         break
426:         finally:
427:             sock.close()
428:         if mac is None:
429:             self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync: no ARP reply from EMP")
430:             return
431:         mac_str = ":".join("%02x" % b for b in mac)
432:         res = subprocess.run(["ip", "link", "set", "dev", self.mgmt_intf, "address", mac_str],
433:                              capture_output=True, text=True)
434:         if res.returncode != 0:
435:             self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync: %s", res.stderr.strip())
436:             return
437:         self.logger.info("EMP MAC %s copied to container %s", mac_str, self.mgmt_intf)

439:     def _login(self, username, password):
440:         """Log in on the console. The first login prompt can come before AAA
441:         is ready, so retry a few times."""
442:         for attempt in range(1, LOGIN_RETRIES + 1):
443:             self.logger.info("vAOS console login attempt %d as %s", attempt, username)
444:             self.tn.write((username + "\r").encode())
445:             ridx, _, _ = self.tn.expect([b"assword:"], 30)
446:             if ridx != 0:
447:                 self.tn.write(b"\r")
448:                 self.tn.expect([b"login:"], 30)
449:                 continue
450:             self.tn.write((password + "\r").encode())
451:             ridx, _, _ = self.tn.expect(
452:                 [PROMPT_RE, rb"Authentication failure|Login incorrect"], 60
453:             )
454:             if ridx == 0:
455:                 self.logger.info("vAOS console login OK")
456:                 return True
457:             self.logger.warning("vAOS login failed, retrying in %ds", LOGIN_RETRY_DELAY)
458:             time.sleep(LOGIN_RETRY_DELAY)
459:             self.tn.write(b"\r")
460:             self.tn.expect([b"login:"], 30)
461:         return False

463:     def _push_config(self, path):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# vrnetlab launcher for Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise OmniSwitch vAOS 8.x.
#
# Boots the VM the way the GNS3 appliance (vAOS8x.gns3a) does:
#   qemu -kernel vAOS8x_bzImage -initrd vAOS8x_ramdisk.gz \
#        -append "console=ttyS0 GNS3=1 inifile=vAOS8x.ini connfile=vAOS8x_fab.con loglevel=0" \
#        -hda vAOS8x.qcow2 -hdb cmm_chassis_info_vAOS8x.tar  (both IDE, e1000 NICs)

import ipaddress
import logging
import os
import re
import signal
import socket
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import vrnetlab


def handle_SIGCHLD(signal, frame):
    os.waitpid(-1, os.WNOHANG)


def handle_SIGTERM(signal, frame):
    sys.exit(0)


signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, handle_SIGTERM)
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, handle_SIGTERM)
signal.signal(signal.SIGCHLD, handle_SIGCHLD)

TRACE_LEVEL_NUM = 9
logging.addLevelName(TRACE_LEVEL_NUM, "TRACE")


def trace(self, message, *args, **kws):
    if self.isEnabledFor(TRACE_LEVEL_NUM):
        self._log(TRACE_LEVEL_NUM, message, args, **kws)


logging.Logger.trace = trace

# Kernel command line copied verbatim from vAOS8x.gns3a.
# (The inifile/connfile configs already live inside the VM disks.)
KERNEL_APPEND = (
    "console=ttyS0 GNS3=1 inifile=vAOS8x.ini connfile=vAOS8x_fab.con loglevel=0"
)

# NIC index (adapter_number) -> OmniSwitch port name, from the vAOS8x.gns3a
# custom_adapters block. Index is the guest NIC enumeration order; index 2 is
# always the EMP (management) port.
#
# We place vrnetlab's management NIC on guest index 2 (= EMP), so EMP is the
# managed interface and every other slot is a usable data port. Result:
#   container ethN -> vAOS port at the matching guest index:
#     eth1 -> 1/1/1   eth2 -> 1/1/2   eth3 -> 1/1/3 ... eth10 -> 1/1/10
#     eth11 -> 1/1/29A   eth12 -> 1/1/30A      (EMP has no container interface)
PORT_MAP = {
    0: "1/1/1",
    1: "1/1/2",
    2: "EMP",      # <- vrnetlab management NIC is mapped here
    3: "1/1/3",
    4: "1/1/4",
    5: "1/1/5",
    6: "1/1/6",
    7: "1/1/7",
    8: "1/1/8",
    9: "1/1/9",
    10: "1/1/10",
    11: "1/1/29A",
    12: "1/1/30A",
}

# guest NIC index reserved for the management NIC (= EMP)
MGMT_NIC_INDEX = 2

# ---- Console bootstrap (EMP auto-configuration) -------------------------
# After boot, launch.py logs in on the serial console and configures EMP.
# All settings are optional environment variables (set them with "env:" in
# the containerlab topology):
#   VAOS_BOOTSTRAP   "false" to skip the bootstrap entirely   (default: true)
#   VAOS_USERNAME    console login     (default: --username, admin)
#   VAOS_PASSWORD    console password  (default: --password, Switch@123)
#   EMP_ROUTES       static routes, "prefix=gateway" separated by commas,
#                    e.g. "192.168.200.0/24=192.168.121.254"
#                    A default route (0.0.0.0/0) is not allowed on EMP and is
#                    skipped; list the specific management prefixes instead.
#   VAOS_STARTUP_CONFIG  path (inside the container) of a startup config to
#                    push after EMP is set. Default: the first non-empty file
#                    of STARTUP_CONFIG_PATHS (ale_vaos kind "startup-config:",
#                    or a generic_vm bind mount at /startup-config.cfg).
#                    Format: AOS CLI, one command per line, as in vcboot.cfg
#                    or "show configuration snapshot". Empty lines and lines
#                    starting with "!" are skipped. Keep the prompt ending
#                    in "->" if the config changes it.
#   VAOS_EXTRA_CMDS  extra CLI commands, separated by ";"
#   VAOS_SAVE        "false" to skip "write memory flash-synchro" (default: true)
# Note: containerlab's own USERNAME/PASSWORD env vars (clab/clab@123) are
# deliberately NOT used: the vAOS image does not know that account.
# Startup config locations: /config/startup-config.cfg is where the containerlab
# ale_vaos kind puts the node startup-config; /startup-config.cfg is for a bind
# mount with the generic_vm kind.
STARTUP_CONFIG_PATHS = ["/config/startup-config.cfg", "/startup-config.cfg"]
# "containerlab save" (ale_vaos kind) drops SAVE_REQUEST in the mounted config
# dir. launch.py then runs "write memory flash-synchro", stores
# "show configuration snapshot" in SAVED_CONFIG and writes "ok" (or the error)
# in SAVE_DONE, which containerlab waits for.
SAVE_REQUEST = "/config/.vaos-save-request"
SAVE_DONE = "/config/.vaos-save-done"
SAVED_CONFIG = "/config/startup-config.cfg"
# async console messages, e.g. "Sat Oct 31 14:02:19 : vcmNi thread INFO message:"
ASYNC_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^\w{3} \w{3} +\d+ \d\d:\d\d:\d\d : ")
LINE_PROMPT_RE = re.compile(r"^[\w.\-]*-> ?$")
LOGIN_RETRIES = 10
LOGIN_RETRY_DELAY = 15
# CLI prompt: a line that starts with "->" or "<name>->". Not anchored at the
# end of the buffer, because async console messages ("+++ Link 1/1/4
# operationally up") can be printed right after the prompt.
PROMPT_RE = rb"(?:^|\n)[\w.\-]*-> ?"
# vAOS shows the login prompt before it accepts configuration. Until it is
# ready, config commands answer with one of these errors: wait and retry.
NOT_READY_RE = (
    rb"has not reached the ready state|not permitted during initialization"
)
READY_RETRY_DELAY = 10
READY_TIMEOUT = 900  # seconds
# Boot is complete when this line shows on the console (same check as the
# GNS3 deploy script). Only then do we log in and configure.
LINK_UP_RE = rb"\+\+\+ Link 1/1/1 operationally up"
BOOT_TIMEOUT = 600  # seconds


class VAOS_vm(vrnetlab.VM):
    def __init__(self, hostname, username, password, nics, conn_mode):
        disk_image = None
        kernel = None
        initrd = None
        hdb = None
        for e in sorted(os.listdir("/")):
            if re.search(r"\.qcow2$", e) and "-overlay" not in e:
                disk_image = "/" + e
            elif re.search(r"bzImage$", e):
                kernel = "/" + e
            elif re.search(r"ramdisk.*\.gz$", e):
                initrd = "/" + e
            elif re.search(r"chassis_info.*\.tar$", e):
                hdb = "/" + e

        if not disk_image:
            raise RuntimeError("No .qcow2 disk image found in /")

        # ram=2048, smp=2 per the gns3a; driveif/ide + e1000 are vrnetlab defaults
        super(VAOS_vm, self).__init__(
            username,
            password,
            disk_image=disk_image,
            ram=2048,
            smp="2",
            driveif="ide",
        )

        self.hostname = hostname
        self.conn_mode = conn_mode
        self.port_map = PORT_MAP
        # expose all defined ports (max); vrnetlab only instantiates NICs for
        # interfaces actually wired in the topology.
        self.num_nics = max(nics, len(PORT_MAP) - 1)
        self.nic_type = "e1000"
        self._log_port_map()

        # Boot via the custom kernel + initrd + append, and attach the second
        # (chassis-info) disk as IDE -> becomes hdb.
        # vrnetlab runs qemu via "shell=True", so the multi-word -append value
        # must be quoted or the shell word-splits it (qemu then treats tokens
        # like "GNS3=1" as bare disk-image args).
        self.qemu_args.extend(
            ["-kernel", kernel, "-initrd", initrd, "-append", '"' + KERNEL_APPEND + '"']
        )
        if hdb:
            self.qemu_args.extend(["-drive", "if=ide,file=" + hdb + ",format=raw"])

        self.logger.info(
            "vAOS boot files: kernel=%s initrd=%s hda=%s hdb=%s",
            kernel, initrd, disk_image, hdb,
        )

    # ---- NIC placement --------------------------------------------------
    # vrnetlab enumerates NICs by PCI slot. To get a clean
    # container-ethN -> vAOS-1/1/N mapping with EMP as the management port, we
    # force every NIC onto bridge pci.1 with explicit, ordered slots and
    # reserve the slot at MGMT_NIC_INDEX for the management NIC (= EMP).

    @staticmethod
    def _eth_to_nic_index(eth_i):
        """container eth index -> guest NIC index (skipping the EMP/mgmt slot)."""
        return eth_i - 1 if eth_i - 1 < MGMT_NIC_INDEX else eth_i

    @staticmethod
    def _set_slot(dev_str, nic_index):
        """Force a -device string onto pci.1 at slot (nic_index + 1)."""
        dev_str = re.sub(r",bus=pci\.\d+", "", dev_str)
        dev_str = re.sub(r",addr=0x[0-9a-fA-F]+", "", dev_str)
        return dev_str + ",bus=pci.1,addr=0x%x" % (nic_index + 1)

    def gen_mgmt(self):
        # Put the management NIC on the EMP slot (guest index 2).
        res = super().gen_mgmt()
        for i, tok in enumerate(res):
            if tok == "-device":
                res[i + 1] = self._set_slot(res[i + 1], MGMT_NIC_INDEX)
        return res

    def gen_nics(self):
        # Re-slot each data NIC so container ethN lands on its target guest index.
        res = super().gen_nics()
        # vrnetlab skips NICs above the highest wired ethN, and the guest numbers
        # NICs in enumeration order. If eth1/eth2 are not wired, the management
        # NIC shifts down and is no longer EMP. Always add unconnected dummies.
        present = set(int(n) for n in re.findall(r"netdev=p(\d+)", " ".join(res)))
        for eth_i in range(1, MGMT_NIC_INDEX + 1):
            if eth_i not in present:
                res.extend([
                    "-device", "%s,netdev=p%02d" % (self.nic_type, eth_i),
                    "-netdev", "socket,id=p%02d,listen=:%d" % (eth_i, 10000 + eth_i),
                ])
        for i, tok in enumerate(res):
            if tok == "-device":
                m = re.search(r"netdev=p(\d+)", res[i + 1])
                if m:
                    eth_i = int(m.group(1))
                    res[i + 1] = self._set_slot(res[i + 1], self._eth_to_nic_index(eth_i))
        return res

    def _log_port_map(self):
        """Log the container-interface <-> vAOS-port mapping for the operator."""
        self.logger.info("vAOS NIC mapping (EMP = vrnetlab management):")
        for nic in sorted(self.port_map):
            port = self.port_map[nic]
            if nic == MGMT_NIC_INDEX:
                src = "vrnetlab management (NAT, or container eth0 in mgmt-passthrough)"
            else:
                eth = nic + 1 if nic < MGMT_NIC_INDEX else nic
                src = "container eth%d" % eth
            self.logger.info("  guest NIC%-2d  vAOS %-8s  <-  %s", nic, port, src)
        self.logger.info("  => eth1=1/1/1, eth2=1/1/2, eth3=1/1/3 ... EMP = management")

    def bootstrap_spin(self):
        """Poll the serial console until the OmniSwitch login prompt appears."""
        if self.spins > 6000:
            self.logger.warning("Too many spins, restarting VM")
            self.stop()
            self.start()
            return

        (ridx, match, res) = self.tn.expect([b"login:"], 1)
        # keep the boot output, in case the link-up line shows before login:
        self._boot_out = getattr(self, "_boot_out", b"") + res
        if match and ridx == 0:
            self.logger.info("vAOS reached login prompt")
            if os.environ.get("VAOS_BOOTSTRAP", "true").lower() != "false":
                try:
                    self.bootstrap_config()
                except Exception as e:
                    self.logger.error("vAOS bootstrap failed: %s", e)
            self.running = True
            self.tn.close()
            return

        if res != b"":
            self.logger.trace("OUTPUT: %s" % res.decode(errors="ignore"))
            self.spins = 0

        self.spins += 1
        return

    # ---- containerlab save ----------------------------------------------

    def work(self):
        super().work()
        if self.running and os.path.exists(SAVE_REQUEST):
            self.save_config()

    def save_config(self):
        """Save the configuration and store a snapshot for containerlab save."""
        self.logger.info("containerlab save requested")
        try:
            os.remove(SAVE_REQUEST)
        except OSError:
            pass
        result = "ok"
        try:
            self.tn.open()
            self.tn.write(b"\r")
            ridx, _, _ = self.tn.expect([PROMPT_RE, b"login:"], 15)
            if ridx == 1:
                username = os.environ.get("VAOS_USERNAME") or self.username
                password = os.environ.get("VAOS_PASSWORD") or self.password
                if not self._login(username, password):
                    raise RuntimeError("could not log in on the console")
            elif ridx != 0:
                raise RuntimeError("no prompt on the console (is a console session open?)")
            self._send("write memory flash-synchro", timeout=180)
            buf = self._send("show configuration snapshot", timeout=120)
            config = self._extract_snapshot(buf)
            if not config.strip():
                raise RuntimeError("empty configuration snapshot")
            with open(SAVED_CONFIG, "w") as f:
                f.write(config)
            self.logger.info("configuration saved to %s", SAVED_CONFIG)
            self.tn.write(b"exit\r")
        except Exception as e:
            result = "error: %s" % e
            self.logger.error("containerlab save failed: %s", e)
        finally:
            try:
                self.tn.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
            with open(SAVE_DONE, "w") as f:
                f.write(result + "\n")

    @staticmethod
    def _extract_snapshot(buf):
        """Keep the configuration lines of "show configuration snapshot".

        Async console messages ("+++ Link 1/1/4 operationally up") can be
        printed in the middle of a line: "spb+++ Link ...\n isis ..." is
        rejoined as "spb isis ...".
        """
        lines = buf.decode(errors="ignore").replace("\r", "").split("\n")
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            if "show configuration snapshot" in line:
                lines = lines[i + 1:]
                break
        out = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(lines):
            line = lines[i]
            i += 1
            if LINE_PROMPT_RE.match(line):
                break  # CLI prompt after the output
            if line.startswith("+++") or ASYNC_HEADER_RE.match(line):
                continue  # async console message on its own line
            pos = line.find("+++")
            if pos > 0:
                # message inserted mid-line: the rest of the line follows it
                while i < len(lines) and lines[i].startswith("+++"):
                    i += 1
                rest = lines[i] if i < len(lines) else ""
                i += 1
                line = line[:pos] + rest
            out.append(line)
        while out and not out[-1].strip():
            out.pop()
        while out and not out[0].strip():
            out.pop(0)
        return "\n".join(out) + "\n"

    # ---- console bootstrap ---------------------------------------------

    def _send(self, cmd, timeout=30):
        """Send one CLI command and wait for the "->" prompt. If vAOS says it
        is not ready yet, wait and send the command again."""
        deadline = time.time() + READY_TIMEOUT
        while True:
            self.logger.info("vAOS> %s", cmd)
            self.tn.write((cmd + "\r").encode())
            ridx, _, buf = self.tn.expect([PROMPT_RE], timeout)
            if ridx != 0:
                self.logger.warning("no prompt after '%s' (continuing)", cmd)
                return buf
            if not re.search(NOT_READY_RE, buf):
                return buf
            if time.time() > deadline:
                self.logger.error("vAOS still not ready after %ds, giving up on '%s'",
                                  READY_TIMEOUT, cmd)
                return buf
            self.logger.info("vAOS not ready yet, retrying in %ds", READY_RETRY_DELAY)
            time.sleep(READY_RETRY_DELAY)

    def _sync_emp_mac(self, emp):
        """mgmt passthrough: copy the EMP MAC address to the container eth0.

        vrnetlab gives the container eth0 the MAC of the VM management NIC, so
        that traffic for the ports kept in the container (5000-5007, serial
        console) is accepted by the container. vAOS does not use that MAC for
        EMP but its own, so the launcher learns it with an ARP probe sent to
        the VM on tap0 and sets it on eth0.
        """
        ip = socket.inet_aton(emp.split("/")[0])
        try:
            with open("/sys/class/net/%s/address" % self.mgmt_intf) as f:
                src = bytes.fromhex(f.read().strip().replace(":", ""))
            # ETH_P_ALL: frames from the VM are redirected to eth0 by tc on tap0
            # ingress; only an ETH_P_ALL socket sees them before that
            sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_PACKET, socket.SOCK_RAW, socket.htons(0x0003))
            sock.bind(("tap0", 0))
            sock.settimeout(1)
        except OSError as e:
            self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync skipped: %s", e)
            return
        # ARP probe: who-has <EMP IP>, sender IP 0.0.0.0
        probe = (b"\xff" * 6 + src + b"\x08\x06"
                 + struct.pack("!HHBBH", 1, 0x0800, 6, 4, 1)
                 + src + b"\x00" * 4 + b"\x00" * 6 + ip)
        mac = None
        deadline = time.time() + 30
        try:
            while mac is None and time.time() < deadline:
                sock.send(probe)
                end = time.time() + 2
                while time.time() < end:
                    try:
                        pkt = sock.recv(2048)
                    except socket.timeout:
                        break
                    # ARP (reply, or gratuitous ARP) sent by the VM from the EMP IP
                    if len(pkt) >= 42 and pkt[12:14] == b"\x08\x06" \
                            and pkt[28:32] == ip and pkt[22:28] != src:
                        mac = pkt[22:28]
                        break
        finally:
            sock.close()
        if mac is None:
            self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync: no ARP reply from EMP")
            return
        mac_str = ":".join("%02x" % b for b in mac)
        res = subprocess.run(["ip", "link", "set", "dev", self.mgmt_intf, "address", mac_str],
                             capture_output=True, text=True)
        if res.returncode != 0:
            self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync: %s", res.stderr.strip())
            return
        self.logger.info("EMP MAC %s copied to container %s", mac_str, self.mgmt_intf)

    def _login(self, username, password):
        """Log in on the console. The first login prompt can come before AAA
        is ready, so retry a few times."""
        for attempt in range(1, LOGIN_RETRIES + 1):
            self.logger.info("vAOS console login attempt %d as %s", attempt, username)
            self.tn.write((username + "\r").encode())
            ridx, _, _ = self.tn.expect([b"assword:"], 30)
            if ridx != 0:
                self.tn.write(b"\r")
                self.tn.expect([b"login:"], 30)
                continue
            self.tn.write((password + "\r").encode())
            ridx, _, _ = self.tn.expect(
                [PROMPT_RE, rb"Authentication failure|Login incorrect"], 60
            )
            if ridx == 0:
                self.logger.info("vAOS console login OK")
                return True
            self.logger.warning("vAOS login failed, retrying in %ds", LOGIN_RETRY_DELAY)
            time.sleep(LOGIN_RETRY_DELAY)
            self.tn.write(b"\r")
            self.tn.expect([b"login:"], 30)
        return False

    def _push_config(self, path):
        """Send a startup config to the CLI, one line at a time."""
        with open(path, errors="ignore") as f:
            lines = [l.strip() for l in f]
        cmds = [l for l in lines if l and not l.startswith("!")]
        self.logger.info("pushing startup config %s (%d commands)", path, len(cmds))
        errors = 0
        for cmd in cmds:
            buf = self._send(cmd, timeout=60)
            if re.search(rb"\bERROR\b", buf):
                errors += 1
                self.logger.warning("startup config line rejected: %s", cmd)
        self.logger.info("startup config pushed: %d commands, %d rejected",
                         len(cmds), errors)

    def bootstrap_config(self):
        """Log in on the serial console and configure EMP (+ optional extras)."""
        username = os.environ.get("VAOS_USERNAME") or self.username
        password = os.environ.get("VAOS_PASSWORD") or self.password

        # EMP address: the node management address (mgmt passthrough), or
        # 10.0.0.15/24, where vrnetlab forwards ssh/snmp/... in NAT mode
        emp = self.mgmt_address_ipv4
        if not emp or emp == "dhcp":
            emp = None
        elif "/" not in emp:
            emp += "/24"

        if re.search(LINK_UP_RE, getattr(self, "_boot_out", b"")):
            self.logger.info("vAOS boot complete (Link 1/1/1 operationally up)")
        else:
            self.logger.info("waiting for '+++ Link 1/1/1 operationally up' (max %ds)",
                             BOOT_TIMEOUT)
            ridx, _, _ = self.tn.expect([LINK_UP_RE], BOOT_TIMEOUT)
            if ridx == 0:
                self.logger.info("vAOS boot complete (Link 1/1/1 operationally up)")
            else:
                self.logger.warning("Link 1/1/1 not up after %ds, trying anyway",
                                    BOOT_TIMEOUT)
        # get a fresh login prompt
        self.tn.write(b"\r")
        self.tn.expect([b"login:"], 30)

        if not self._login(username, password):
            raise RuntimeError("could not log in as %s" % username)

        hostname = os.environ.get("HOSTNAME") or self.hostname
        self._send("system name %s" % hostname)
        self._send('session prompt default "%s->"' % hostname)

        if emp:
            self._send("ip interface emp address %s" % emp)
            if self.mgmt_passthrough:
                self._sync_emp_mac(emp)
        else:
            self.logger.info("no EMP address to configure (DHCP mode)")

        for route in filter(None, os.environ.get("EMP_ROUTES", "").split(",")):
            prefix, _, gw = route.strip().partition("=")
            try:
                net = ipaddress.IPv4Network(prefix.strip(), strict=False)
                gw_ip = ipaddress.IPv4Address(gw.strip())
            except ValueError:
                self.logger.warning("ignoring malformed EMP_ROUTES entry '%s'", route)
                continue
            if net.prefixlen == 0:
                self.logger.warning(
                    "ignoring EMP_ROUTES entry '%s': a default route is not "
                    "allowed on EMP, use specific prefixes", route)
                continue
            self._send("ip static-route %s gateway %s" % (net, gw_ip))

        cfg_path = os.environ.get("VAOS_STARTUP_CONFIG")
        if cfg_path and not os.path.isfile(cfg_path):
            self.logger.warning("startup config %s not found in the container", cfg_path)
        for path in ([cfg_path] if cfg_path else STARTUP_CONFIG_PATHS):
            if path and os.path.isfile(path) and os.path.getsize(path) > 0:
                self._push_config(path)
                break

        for cmd in os.environ.get("VAOS_EXTRA_CMDS", "").split(";"):
            if cmd.strip():
                self._send(cmd.strip())

        if os.environ.get("VAOS_SAVE", "true").lower() != "false":
            self._send("write memory flash-synchro", timeout=180)

        self._send("show ip interface")
        self.logger.info("vAOS bootstrap done (EMP %s)", emp)


class VAOS(vrnetlab.VR):
    def __init__(self, hostname, username, password, nics, conn_mode):

def __init__(
        self,
        username,
        password,
        disk_image="",
        num=0,
        ram=4096,
        driveif="ide",
        provision_pci_bus=True,
        cpu="host",
        smp="1",
        mgmt_passthrough=False,
        mgmt_intf="eth0",
        mgmt_dhcp=False,
        min_dp_nics=0,
        data_intf_prefix="eth",
        arch="x86_64",
    ):
        self.arch = arch

        # configure logging
        self.logger = logging.getLogger()

        """
        Configure Scrapli logger to only be INFO level.
        Scrapli uses 'scrapli' logger by default, and
        will write all channel i/o as DEBUG log level.
        """
        self.scrapli_logger = logging.getLogger("scrapli")

        scrapli_log_level = (
            logging.DEBUG
            if os.getenv("DEBUG_SCRAPLI", "false").lower() == "true"
            else logging.INFO
        )
        self.scrapli_logger.setLevel(scrapli_log_level)

        # init scrapli_tn -- main telnet device
        scrapli_tn_dev = {
            "host": "127.0.0.1",
            "port": 5000 + num,
            "auth_bypass": True,
            "auth_strict_key": False,
            "transport": "telnet",
            "timeout_socket": 3600,
            "timeout_transport": 3600,
            "timeout_ops": 3600,
        }

        self.scrapli_tn = Driver(**scrapli_tn_dev)

        # init scrapli_qm_dev -- qemu monitor device
        scrapli_qm_dev = {
            "host": "127.0.0.1",
            "port": 4000 + num,
            "auth_bypass": True,
            "auth_strict_key": False,
            "transport": "telnet",
            "timeout_socket": 3600,
            "timeout_transport": 3600,
            "timeout_ops": 3600,
        }

        self.scrapli_qm = Driver(**scrapli_qm_dev)

        # telnetlib-compatible facades the launchers use: self.tn drives the
        # serial console, self.qm the qemu monitor.
        self.tn = _Console(self.scrapli_tn)
        self.qm = _Console(self.scrapli_qm)

        # username / password to configure
        self.username = username
        self.password = password

        self.num = num
        self.image = disk_image

        self.running = False
        self.spins = 0
        self.p = None

        self._ram = ram
        self._cpu = cpu
        self._smp = smp
        self.mgmt_intf = os.environ.get("CLAB_MGMT_INTF", mgmt_intf)

        # various settings
        # start() appends the UUID resolved by the uuid property to the qemu command.
        self._uuid = None
        self.fake_start_date = None
        self.nic_type = "e1000"
        self.num_nics = 0
        self.num_mgmt_nics = 1
        # whether the container/VM can be started without the mgmt interface
        self.supports_mgmtless = False
        # number of nics that are actually *provisioned* (as in nics that will be added to container)
        self.num_provisioned_nics = int(os.environ.get("CLAB_INTFS", 0))
        # "highest" provisioned nic num -- used for making sure we can allocate nics without needing
        # to have them allocated sequential from eth1
        self.highest_provisioned_nic_num = 0

        # Whether the management interface is pass-through or host-forwarded.
        # Host-forwarded is the original vrnetlab mode where a VM gets a static IP for its management address,
        # which **does not** match the eth0 interface of a container.
        # In pass-through mode the VM container uses the same IP as the container's eth0 interface and transparently forwards traffic between the two interfaces.
        # See https://github.com/hellt/vrnetlab/issues/286
        self.mgmt_passthrough = (
            os.environ.get("CLAB_MGMT_PASSTHROUGH", "").lower() == "true"
            if os.environ.get("CLAB_MGMT_PASSTHROUGH")
            else mgmt_passthrough
        )

        # Check if CLAB_MGMT_DHCP environment variable is set
        self.mgmt_dhcp = (
            os.environ.get("CLAB_MGMT_DHCP", "").lower() == "true"
            if os.environ.get("CLAB_MGMT_DHCP")
            else mgmt_dhcp
        )

        # Check if CLAB_INTF_PREFIX environment variable is set
        self.data_intf_prefix = os.environ.get("CLAB_INTF_PREFIX", data_intf_prefix)

        # Populate management IP and gateway
        # If CLAB_MGMT_DHCP environment variable is set, we assume that a DHCP client
        # inside of the VM will take care about setting the management IP and gateway.
        if self.mgmt_passthrough:
            if self.mgmt_dhcp:
                self.mgmt_address_ipv4 = "dhcp"
                self.mgmt_address_ipv6 = "dhcp"
                self.mgmt_gw_ipv4 = "dhcp"
                self.mgmt_gw_ipv6 = "dhcp"
            else:
                self.mgmt_address_ipv4, self.mgmt_address_ipv6 = self.get_mgmt_address()
                self.mgmt_gw_ipv4, self.mgmt_gw_ipv6 = self.get_mgmt_gw()
        else:
            self.mgmt_address_ipv4 = "10.0.0.15/24"
            self.mgmt_address_ipv6 = "2001:db8::2/64"
            self.mgmt_gw_ipv4 = "10.0.0.2"
            self.mgmt_gw_ipv6 = "2001:db8::1"

        self.insuffucient_nics = False
        self.min_nics = 0
        # if an image needs minimum amount of dataplane nics to bootup, specify
        if min_dp_nics:
            self.min_nics = min_dp_nics

        # management subnet properties, defaults
        self.mgmt_subnet = "10.0.0.0/24"
        self.mgmt_host_ip = 2
        self.mgmt_guest_ip = 15

        #  Default TCP ports forwarded (TODO tune per platform):
        #  80    - http
        #  443   - https
        #  830   - netconf
        #  6030  - gnmi/gnoi arista
        #  8080  - sonic gnmi/gnoi, other http apis
        #  9339  - iana gnmi/gnoi
        #  32767 - gnmi/gnoi juniper
        #  50051 - cisco nx-os gnmi/gnoi
        #  57400 - nokia gnmi/gnoi
        self.mgmt_tcp_ports = [80, 443, 830, 6030, 8080, 9339, 32767, 50051, 57400]

        # we setup pci bus by default
        self.provision_pci_bus = provision_pci_bus
        self.nics_per_pci_bus = 26  # tested to work with XRv
        self.smbios = []

        self.start_nic_eth_idx = 1

        # wait_pattern is the pattern we wait on the serial connection when pushing config commands
        self.wait_pattern = "#"

        # Check if we're restoring from snapshot
        snapshot_disk = f"/snapshot-data/vm{self.num}/disk.qcow2"
        snapshot_state = f"/snapshot-data/vm{self.num}/state.img"
        snapshot_metadata = f"/snapshot-data/vm{self.num}/metadata.json"
        restoring_snapshot = os.path.exists(snapshot_disk) and os.path.exists(
            snapshot_state
        )

        # Load snapshot metadata if restoring
        self.snapshot_metadata = None
        if restoring_snapshot:
            self.logger.info(f"Restoring from snapshot")
            self.logger.info(f"Snapshot disk: {snapshot_disk}")
            self.logger.info(f"Snapshot state: {snapshot_state}")

            if os.path.exists(snapshot_metadata):
                with open(snapshot_metadata, "r") as f:
                    self.snapshot_metadata = json.load(f)
                self.logger.info(f"Loaded snapshot metadata: {self.snapshot_metadata}")

                # Restore secondary disks
                if "secondary_disks" in self.snapshot_metadata:
                    for disk in self.snapshot_metadata["secondary_disks"]:
                        self.logger.info(f"Restoring secondary disk: {disk}")
                        shutil.copy2(
                            os.path.join(f"/snapshot-data/vm{self.num}", disk), disk
                        )

            overlay_disk_image = f"/snapshot-data/vm{self.num}/disk-overlay.qcow2"
            base_disk = snapshot_disk
            base_format = "qcow2"
        else:
            overlay_disk_image = re.sub(r"(\.[^.]+$)", r"-overlay\1", disk_image)
            if hasattr(self, "role"):
                tokens = overlay_disk_image.split(".")
                tokens[0] = tokens[0] + "-" + self.role + str(self.num)
                overlay_disk_image = ".".join(tokens)
            base_disk = disk_image
            base_format = self._overlay_disk_image_format()

        if not os.path.exists(overlay_disk_image):
            self.logger.debug(f"Creating overlay disk image: {overlay_disk_image}")
            run_command(
                [
                    "qemu-img",
                    "create",
                    "-f",
                    "qcow2",
                    "-F",
                    base_format,
                    "-b",
                    base_disk,
                    overlay_disk_image,
                ]
            )

        machine = (
            "pc"
            if self.arch == "x86_64"
            else "virt,virtualization=on -accel tcg,tb-size=128"
        )

        # Build qemu args
        self.qemu_args = [
            f"qemu-system-{self.arch}",
            "-display",
            "none",
            "-machine",
            machine,
            f"-chardev socket,id=monitor0,host=::,port=40{self.num:02d},server=on,wait=off",
            "-monitor chardev:monitor0",
            f"-chardev socket,id=serial0,host=::,port=50{self.num:02d},server=on,wait=off,telnet=on",
            "-serial chardev:serial0",
            "-m",  # memory
            str(self.ram),
            "-cpu",  # cpu type
            self.cpu,
            "-smp",
            self.smp,  # cpu core configuration
        ]

        # Always use -drive to create the disk device - migration requires exact device match
        self.qemu_args.extend(["-drive", f"if={driveif},file={overlay_disk_image}"])

        # If restoring from snapshot, add -incoming parameter
        if restoring_snapshot:
            self.qemu_args.extend(["-incoming", "defer"])

        # add additional qemu args if they were provided
        if self.qemu_additional_args:
            self.qemu_args.extend(self.qemu_additional_args)

        # enable hardware assist if KVM is available
        if os.path.exists("/dev/kvm"):
            self.qemu_args.insert(1, "-enable-kvm")

    def start(self):
        # self.logger.info("Starting %s" % self.__class__.__name__)
        self.logger.info("START ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES".center(60, "-"))
        for var, value in sorted(os.environ.items()):
            self.logger.info(f"{var}: {value}")
        self.logger.info("END ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES".center(60, "-"))

        self.logger.info(
            f"Launching {self.__class__.__name__} arch {self.arch} with {self.smp} SMP/VCPU and {self.ram} M of RAM"
        )

        # give nice colours. Red if disabled, Green if enabled
        mgmt_passthrough_coloured = format_bool_color(
            self.mgmt_passthrough, "Enabled", "Disabled"
        )

        self.logger.info(f"Transparent mgmt interface: {mgmt_passthrough_coloured}")

        self.start_time = datetime.datetime.now()

        cmd = list(self.qemu_args)

        # uuid
        if self.uuid:
            cmd.extend(["-uuid", self.uuid])

        # do we have a fake start date?
        if self.fake_start_date:
            cmd.extend(["-rtc", "base=" + self.fake_start_date])

def gen_mgmt(self):
        """Generate qemu args for the mgmt interface(s)

        Default TCP ports forwarded:
          80    - http
          443   - https
          830   - netconf
          6030  - gnmi/gnoi arista
          8080  - sonic gnmi/gnoi, other http apis
          9339  - iana gnmi/gnoi
          32767 - gnmi/gnoi juniper
          50051 - cisco nx-os gnmi/gnoi
          57400 - nokia gnmi/gnoi
        """
        if self.mgmt_host_ip + 1 >= self.mgmt_guest_ip:
            self.logger.error(
                "Guest IP (%s) must be at least 2 higher than host IP(%s)",
                self.mgmt_guest_ip,
                self.mgmt_host_ip,
            )

        network = ipaddress.ip_network(self.mgmt_subnet)
        host = str(network[self.mgmt_host_ip])
        dns = str(network[self.mgmt_host_ip + 1])
        guest = str(network[self.mgmt_guest_ip])

        res = []
        res.append("-device")

        # If restoring from snapshot, use the saved management MAC address
        if (
            self.snapshot_metadata
            and "mac_addresses" in self.snapshot_metadata
            and len(self.snapshot_metadata["mac_addresses"]) > 0
        ):
            self.mgmt_mac = self.snapshot_metadata["mac_addresses"][0]
            self.logger.info(f"Using saved management MAC: {self.mgmt_mac}")
        else:
            self.mgmt_mac = self.get_mgmt_mac()

        res.append(self.nic_type + f",netdev=p00,mac={self.mgmt_mac}")
        res.append("-netdev")

        if self.mgmt_passthrough:
            # mgmt interface is passthrough - we just create a normal mirred tap interface
            res.append(
                "tap,id=p00,ifname=tap0,script=/etc/tc-tap-mgmt-ifup,downscript=no"
            )
            self.create_tc_tap_mgmt_ifup()
        else:
            # mgmt interface is host-forwarded - we use qemu user mode network
            # with hostfwd rules to forward ports from the host to the guest
            res.append(
                f"user,id=p00,net={self.mgmt_subnet},host={host},dns={dns},dhcpstart={guest},"
                + f"hostfwd=tcp:0.0.0.0:22-{guest}:22,"  # ssh
                + f"hostfwd=udp:0.0.0.0:161-{guest}:161,"  # snmp
                + (
                    ",".join(
                        [
                            f"hostfwd=tcp:0.0.0.0:{p}-{guest}:{p}"
                            for p in self.mgmt_tcp_ports
                        ]
                    )
                )
                + ",tftp=/tftpboot"
            )

        return res

    def get_mgmt_address(self):
        """Returns the IPv4 and IPv6 address of the eth0 interface of the container"""
        stdout, _ = run_command(["ip", "--json", "address", "show", "dev", "eth0"])
        command_json = json.loads(stdout.decode("utf-8"))
        intf_addrinfos = command_json[0]["addr_info"]
        mgmt_cidr_v4 = None
        mgmt_cidr_v6 = None
        for addrinfo in intf_addrinfos:
            if addrinfo["family"] == "inet" and addrinfo["scope"] == "global":
                mgmt_address_v4 = addrinfo["local"]
                mgmt_prefixlen_v4 = addrinfo["prefixlen"]
                mgmt_cidr_v4 = mgmt_address_v4 + "/" + str(mgmt_prefixlen_v4)
            if addrinfo["family"] == "inet6" and addrinfo["scope"] == "global":
                mgmt_address_v6 = addrinfo["local"]
                mgmt_prefixlen_v6 = addrinfo["prefixlen"]
                mgmt_cidr_v6 = mgmt_address_v6 + "/" + str(mgmt_prefixlen_v6)

        if not mgmt_cidr_v4:
            raise ValueError("No IPv4 address set on management interface eth0!")

        return mgmt_cidr_v4, mgmt_cidr_v6

    def get_mgmt_gw(self):
        """Returns the IPv4 and IPv6 default gateways of the container, used for generating the management default route"""
        stdout_v4, _ = run_command(["ip", "--json", "-4", "route", "show", "default"])
        command_json_v4 = json.loads(stdout_v4.decode("utf-8"))
        try:
            mgmt_gw_v4 = command_json_v4[0]["gateway"]
        except IndexError as e:
            raise IndexError(
                "No default gateway route on management interface eth0!"
            ) from e

        stdout_v6, _ = run_command(["ip", "--json", "-6", "route", "show", "default"])
        command_json_v6 = json.loads(stdout_v6.decode("utf-8"))
        try:
            mgmt_gw_v6 = command_json_v6[0]["gateway"]
        except IndexError:
            mgmt_gw_v6 = None

        return mgmt_gw_v4, mgmt_gw_v6

    def get_intf_mac(self, intf_name: str) -> str:
        """Get the MAC address of a container interface

        Returns the MAC address of the specified interface, or None if not found.
        This is used to sync VM NIC MAC addresses with container interface MAC addresses
        for proper macvlan bridge mode operation.
        """
        try:
            stdout, _ = run_command(["ip", "--json", "link", "show", "dev", intf_name])

    def gen_nics(self):

        start_eth = self.start_nic_eth_idx

    ):
        """Wait for something on the serial port and then send command

NO! `bytes` has `.decode()`, but a compiled pattern does not. So `PROMPT_RE = re.compile(...)` passed to `self.tn.expect([PROMPT_RE], 15)` will raise `AttributeError: 're.Pattern' object has no attribute 'decode'`.

Wait — check: `for i, pat in enumerate(regex_list): match = re.search(pat.decode(), buf.decode(...))`. If `pat` is a compiled pattern, `pat.decode()` → AttributeError. Unless the compiled pattern wraps... no. So this is a real P1/P2 bug: every call to `self.tn.expect([PROMPT_RE], ...)` in launch.py raises AttributeError:

- `save_config`: `self.tn.expect([PROMPT_RE, b"login:"], 15)` → first pattern is compiled → AttributeError → caught by `except Exception` → result = "error: ..." → SAVE_DONE written with error. So containerlab save always fails.

Hold on — is this really how other launchers use it? Let me check how other launchers call expect. E.g., grep for `re.compile` in other launchers and how they pass to `self.tn.expect`. Many vrnetlab launchers pass raw byte strings. Let me verify that no other launcher passes compiled patterns, and confirm `_Console.expect` is what launch.py's `self.tn` is.

`self.tn = _Console(self.scrapli_tn)` (line 280). Yes, launch.py's `self.tn` is `_Console`. And `_Console.expect` does `pat.decode()`.

So compiled patterns break. This is a genuine P1: bootstrap always fails with AttributeError. display.text:
# vrnetlab - VR Network Lab

This is a fork of the original [plajjan/vrnetlab](https://github.com/plajjan/vrnetlab)
project and was created specifically to make vrnetlab-based images runnable by
[containerlab](https://containerlab.srlinux.dev).

The documentation provided in this fork only explains the parts that have been
changed from the upstream project. To get a general overview of the vrnetlab
project itself, consider reading the [docs of the upstream repo](https://github.com/vrnetlab/vrnetlab/blob/master/README.md).

## What is this fork about?

At [containerlab](https://containerlab.srlinux.dev) we needed to have
[a way to run virtual routers](https://containerlab.dev/manual/vrnetlab/)
alongside the containerized Network Operating Systems.

Vrnetlab provides perfect machinery to package most-common routing VMs in
container packaging. What upstream vrnetlab doesn't do, though, is create
datapaths between the VMs in a "container-native" way.

Vrnetlab relies on a separate VM ([vr-xcon](https://github.com/vrnetlab/vrnetlab/tree/master/vr-xcon))
to stitch sockets exposed on each container and that doesn't play well with the
regular ways of interconnecting container workloads.

This fork adds the additional option `connection-mode` to the `launch.py` script
of supported VMs. The `connection-mode` option controls how vrnetlab creates
datapaths for launched VMs.

The `connection-mode` values make it possible to run vrnetlab containers with
networking that doesn't require a separate container and is native to tools such
as docker.

### Container-native networking?

Yes, the term is bloated. What it actually means is this fork makes it possible
to add interfaces to a container hosting a qemu VM and vrnetlab will recognize
those interfaces and stitch them with the VM interfaces.

With this you can, for example, add veth pairs between containers as you would
normally and vrnetlab will make sure these ports get mapped to your routers'
ports. In essence, that allows you to work with your vrnetlab containers like a
normal container and get the datapath working in the same "native" way.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Although the changes we made here are of a general purpose and you can run
> vrnetlab routers with docker CLI or any other container runtime, the purpose
> of this work was to couple vrnetlab with containerlab.
>
> With this being said, we recommend the readers start their journey from
> this [documentation entry](https://containerlab.dev/manual/vrnetlab/)
> which will show you how easy it is to run routers in a containerized setting.

## Connection modes

As mentioned above, the major change this fork brings is the ability to run
vrnetlab containers without requiring [vr-xcon](https://github.com/vrnetlab/vrnetlab/tree/master/vr-xcon)
and instead uses container-native networking.

For containerlab the default connection mode value is `connection-mode=tc`.
With this particular mode we use **tc-mirred** redirects to stitch a container's
interfaces `eth1+` with the ports of the qemu VM running inside.

![diagram showing network connections via tc redirects](https://gitlab.com/rdodin/pics/-/wikis/uploads/4d31c06e6258e70edc887b17e0e758e0/image.png)

Using tc redirection (tc-mirred) we get a transparent pipe between a container's
interfaces and those of the VMs running within.

We scrambled through many connection alternatives, which are described in
[this post](https://netdevops.me/2021/transparently-redirecting-packetsframes-between-interfaces/),
but tc redirect (tc-mirred :star:) works best of all.

### Mode List

Full list of connection mode values:

| Connection Mode | LACP Support        | Description |
| --------------- | :-----------------: | :---------- |
| tc-mirred       | :white_check_mark:  | Creates a linux bridge and attaches `eth` and `tap` interfaces to it. Cleanest solution for point-to-point links.
| bridge          | :last_quarter_moon: | No additional kernel modules and has native qemu/libvirt support. Does not support passing STP. Requires restricting `MAC_PAUSE` frames in order to support LACP.
| ovs-bridge      | :white_check_mark:  | Same as a regular bridge, but uses OvS (Open vSwitch).
| macvtap         | :x:                 | Requires mounting entire `/dev` to a container namespace. Needs file descriptor manipulation due to no native qemu support.

## Management interface

There are two types of management connectivity for NOS VMs: _pass-through_ and _host-forwarded_ (legacy) management interfaces.

_Pass-through management_ interfaces allows the use of the assigned management IP within the NOS VM, management traffic is transparently passed through to the VM, and the NOS configuration can accurately reflect the management IP. However, it is no longer possible to send or receive traffic directly in the vrnetlab container (e.g. for installing additional packages within the container), other than to pre-defined exceptions, such as the QEMU serial port on TCP port 5000.

NOSes defaulting to _pass-through_ management interfaces are:

we are gathering feedback on this, and will update this list as feedback is received. Please contact us in [Discord](https://discord.gg/vAyddtaEV9) or open up an issue here if you have found any issues when trying the passthrough mode.
* Fortinet/Fortigate

In case of _host-forwarded_ management interfaces, certain ports are forwarded to the NOS VM IP, which is always 10.0.0.15/24. The management gateway in this case is 10.0.0.2/24, and outgoing traffic is NATed to the container management IP. This management interface connection mode does not allow for traffic such as LLDP to pass through the management interface.

NOSes defaulting to _host-forwarded_ management interfaces are:

* all current systems

It is possible to change from the default management interface mode by setting the `CLAB_MGMT_PASSTHROUGH` environment variable to 'true' or 'false', however, it is left up to the user to provide a startup configuration compatible with the requested mode.

## Resetting Virtual Routers

You can force-reset all or a subset of VR component VMs by creating a file named `reset` in the root path (`/`) of the container. This triggers a qemu-monitor `system_reset` command to the specified VM(s), which acts like a hardware reset button without disrupting existing qemu VM properties (interfaces, disks...). Useful for recovering VMs in a hung state or for testing scenarios.

 - To reset the VR (all component VMs), create an empty `/reset` file.
 - To reset a subset of the VR VMs, write a comma-separated list of VM numbers to the `/reset` file.

Usage examples:
```bash
sudo docker exec container_name_or_id touch /reset #reset VR (all component VMs)
sudo docker exec container_name_or_id sh -c 'echo "0" > /reset' #reset VM 0
sudo docker exec container_name_or_id sh -c 'echo "1,2" > /reset' #reset VM 1 & VM 2
```

> **Note:**  
> VM numbers correspond to the internal numbering used by vrnetlab (typically starting from 0).

## Snapshotting virtual routers

You can snapshot all VMs in a running container by adding a `/snapshot-save` file to the root path of the container.
This prompts the container to pause the VM and save VM states, disk overlays and metadata to `/snapshot-output.tar` before resuming the VM.
Using this snapshot file you can start nodes using the same image up to the exact same state the VM had when you took the snapshot.

This can save a lot of time for workflows that rely on VMs reaching a known-good state.

**Basic usage**
```bash
# Start a VM and wait for it to boot
docker run -d --name node --privileged vrnetlab/{your-image}

# Create snapshot
docker exec node touch /snapshot-save

# Extract snapshot tar
docker cp node:/snapshot-output.tar ./snapshot.tar

# Start new container with snapshot
docker run -d --name restored-node --privileged \ 
  -e RESTORE_SNAPSHOT=1 \ 
  -v $(pwd)/snapshot.tar:/snapshot.tar:ro \ 
  vrnetlab/{your-image}
```

## Which vrnetlab routers are supported?

Since the changes we made in this fork are VM specific, we added a few popular
routing products:

* Arista vEOS
* Cisco XRd vRouter
* Cisco XRv9k
* Cisco XRv
* Cisco FTDv
* Juniper vMX
* Juniper vSRX
* Juniper vJunos-switch
* Juniper vJunos-router
* Juniper vJunosEvolved
* Nokia SR OS
* OpenBSD
* FreeBSD
* Ubuntu

The rest are left untouched and can be contributed back by the community.

## Does the build process change?

No. You build the images exactly as before.

        )

        self.hostname = hostname
        self.conn_mode = conn_mode
        self.num_nics = 33
        self.nic_type = "e1000"

    def wait_write_config(self, cmd, wait="#", retries=30, delay=5, error_patterns=None):
        """Execute command with retry logic for transient VOSS boot states.

        Retries when the response contains any of the strings in error_patterns
        or the generic 'configuration load' rejection message.
        """
        retry_patterns = ["configuration load"]
        if error_patterns:
            retry_patterns.extend(error_patterns)

        for attempt in range(retries):
            self.tn.write(f"{cmd}\r".encode())
            try:
                res = self.tn.read_until(wait.encode(), timeout=30)
                response_str = res.decode(errors="ignore")

                matched = next(
                    (p for p in retry_patterns if p.lower() in response_str.lower()),
                    None,
                )
                if matched:
                    self.logger.info(
                        f"Retryable response ({matched!r}) for '{cmd}', attempt {attempt + 1}/{retries}, waiting {delay}s..."
                    )
                    time.sleep(delay)
                    continue

                return
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.warning(f"Timeout waiting for prompt after '{cmd}': {e}")
                if attempt < retries - 1:
                    time.sleep(delay)
                continue

        self.logger.error(f"Command '{cmd}' failed after {retries} retries")

    def bootstrap_spin(self):
        """ This function should be called periodically to do work.
        """

        if self.spins > 300:
            # too many spins with no result ->  give up
            self.stop()
            self.start()
            return

        (_, match, res) = self.tn.expect([rb'ogin:'], 1)

        if match:  # got a match!
            time.sleep(1)
            self.wait_write(cmd="", wait=None)
            self.wait_write(cmd="rwa", wait="ogin:")
            self.wait_write(cmd="rwa", wait="assword")
            # First login with the default rwa/rwa forces a password change
            self.wait_write(cmd=self.password, wait="assword")
            self.wait_write(cmd=self.password, wait="assword")
            self.wait_write(cmd="", wait=">")

            # run main config!
            self.logger.info("Running bootstrap_config()")
            self.bootstrap_config()
            self.startup_config()
            time.sleep(1)
            # close telnet connection
            self.tn.close()
            # startup time?
            startup_time = datetime.datetime.now() - self.start_time
            self.logger.info("Startup complete in: %s" % startup_time)

            return

        # booting, so let's give it some more time
        if res != b"":
            self.logger.trace("OUTPUT: %s" % res.decode())
            # reset spins if we saw some output
            self.spins = 0

        self.spins += 1

        return


    def bootstrap_config(self):
        """ Do the actual bootstrap config
        """
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="enable", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="configure terminal", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd=f"sys name {self.hostname}", wait="#")
        # VOSS boots in ZTP mode with "mgmt dhcp-client cycle", which keeps
        # requesting DHCP on the oob and onboarding VLAN interfaces. Without a
        # DHCP server (transparent mgmt) it puts a 169.254.x.x link-local address
        # on oob every cycle, so disable it before configuring oob statically.
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="no mgmt dhcp-client", wait="#")
        # Recreate the oob instance, then configure 10.0.0.15/24 (qemu user-mode
        # network) or the container's address (transparent mgmt) statically.
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="no mgmt oob", wait="(y/n) ?")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="y", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="mgmt oob", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd=f"ip address {self.mgmt_address_ipv4}", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(
            cmd=f"ip route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop {self.mgmt_gw_ipv4}", wait="#"
        )
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="enable", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="exit", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(
            cmd=f"username add {self.username} level rwa enable", wait="assword"
        )
        self.wait_write_config(cmd=self.password, wait="assword")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd=self.password, wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="exit", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="save config", wait="#")

    def startup_config(self):
        if not os.path.exists(STARTUP_CONFIG_FILE):
            self.logger.trace(f"Startup config file {STARTUP_CONFIG_FILE} not found")
            return
        if not self.mgmt_passthrough:
            # qemu user-mode network serves /tftpboot on 10.0.0.2.
            # "source" always runs the file from privileged exec mode, so it must
            # enter config mode itself, like a saved VOSS config does.
            with open(STARTUP_CONFIG_FILE) as file:
                config = file.read()
            commands = [line.strip() for line in config.splitlines()]
            commands = [line for line in commands if line and not line.startswith("#")]
            if not (commands and commands[0].startswith("conf")):
                config = f"configure terminal\n{config}\nend\n"
            with open("/tftpboot/containerlab.cfg", "w") as file:
                file.write(config)
            self.wait_write_config(
                cmd="copy 10.0.0.2:containerlab.cfg /intflash/containerlab.cfg", wait="#"
            )
            self.wait_write_config(cmd="source /intflash/containerlab.cfg", wait="#")
            self.wait_write_config(cmd="save config", wait="#")
            return

        # Transparent mgmt: no TFTP server reachable, push the config over the
        # serial console instead.
        with open(STARTUP_CONFIG_FILE) as file:
            config_lines = [line.rstrip() for line in file.readlines()]

        self.logger.info(f"Writing lines from {STARTUP_CONFIG_FILE}")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="configure terminal", wait="#")
        for line in config_lines:
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            self.wait_write_config(cmd=line, wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="end", wait="#")
        self.wait_write_config(cmd="save config", wait="#")

class VAOS_vm(vrnetlab.VM):
    def __init__(self, hostname, username, password, nics, conn_mode):
        disk_image = None
        kernel = None
        initrd = None
        hdb = None
        for e in sorted(os.listdir("/")):
            if re.search(r"\.qcow2$", e) and "-overlay" not in e:
                disk_image = "/" + e
            elif re.search(r"bzImage$", e):
                kernel = "/" + e
            elif re.search(r"ramdisk.*\.gz$", e):
                initrd = "/" + e
            elif re.search(r"chassis_info.*\.tar$", e):
                hdb = "/" + e

        if not disk_image:
            raise RuntimeError("No .qcow2 disk image found in /")

        # ram=2048, smp=2 per the gns3a; driveif/ide + e1000 are vrnetlab defaults
        super(VAOS_vm, self).__init__(
            username,
            password,
            disk_image=disk_image,
            ram=2048,
            smp="2",
            driveif="ide",
        )

        self.hostname = hostname
        self.conn_mode = conn_mode
        self.port_map = PORT_MAP
        # expose all defined ports (max); vrnetlab only instantiates NICs for
        # interfaces actually wired in the topology.
        self.num_nics = max(nics, len(PORT_MAP) - 1)
        self.nic_type = "e1000"
        self._log_port_map()

        # Boot via the custom kernel + initrd + append, and attach the second
        # (chassis-info) disk as IDE -> becomes hdb.
        # vrnetlab runs qemu via "shell=True", so the multi-word -append value
        # must be quoted or the shell word-splits it (qemu then treats tokens
        # like "GNS3=1" as bare disk-image args).
        self.qemu_args.extend(
            ["-kernel", kernel, "-initrd", initrd, "-append", '"' + KERNEL_APPEND + '"']
        )
        if hdb:
            self.qemu_args.extend(["-drive", "if=ide,file=" + hdb + ",format=raw"])

        self.logger.info(
            "vAOS boot files: kernel=%s initrd=%s hda=%s hdb=%s",
            kernel, initrd, disk_image, hdb,
        )

    # ---- NIC placement --------------------------------------------------
    # vrnetlab enumerates NICs by PCI slot. To get a clean
    # container-ethN -> vAOS-1/1/N mapping with EMP as the management port, we
    # force every NIC onto bridge pci.1 with explicit, ordered slots and
    # reserve the slot at MGMT_NIC_INDEX for the management NIC (= EMP).

    @staticmethod
    def _eth_to_nic_index(eth_i):
        """container eth index -> guest NIC index (skipping the EMP/mgmt slot)."""
        return eth_i - 1 if eth_i - 1 < MGMT_NIC_INDEX else eth_i

    @staticmethod
    def _set_slot(dev_str, nic_index):
        """Force a -device string onto pci.1 at slot (nic_index + 1)."""
        dev_str = re.sub(r",bus=pci\.\d+", "", dev_str)
        dev_str = re.sub(r",addr=0x[0-9a-fA-F]+", "", dev_str)
        return dev_str + ",bus=pci.1,addr=0x%x" % (nic_index + 1)

    def gen_mgmt(self):
        # Put the management NIC on the EMP slot (guest index 2).

def _sync_emp_mac(self, emp):
        """mgmt passthrough: copy the EMP MAC address to the container eth0.

        vrnetlab gives the container eth0 the MAC of the VM management NIC, so
        that traffic for the ports kept in the container (5000-5007, serial
        console) is accepted by the container. vAOS does not use that MAC for
        EMP but its own, so the launcher learns it with an ARP probe sent to
        the VM on tap0 and sets it on eth0.
        """
        ip = socket.inet_aton(emp.split("/")[0])
        try:
            with open("/sys/class/net/%s/address" % self.mgmt_intf) as f:
                src = bytes.fromhex(f.read().strip().replace(":", ""))
            # ETH_P_ALL: frames from the VM are redirected to eth0 by tc on tap0
            # ingress; only an ETH_P_ALL socket sees them before that
            sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_PACKET, socket.SOCK_RAW, socket.htons(0x0003))
            sock.bind(("tap0", 0))
            sock.settimeout(1)
        except OSError as e:
            self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync skipped: %s", e)
            return
        # ARP probe: who-has <EMP IP>, sender IP 0.0.0.0
        probe = (b"\xff" * 6 + src + b"\x08\x06"
                 + struct.pack("!HHBBH", 1, 0x0800, 6, 4, 1)
                 + src + b"\x00" * 4 + b"\x00" * 6 + ip)
        mac = None
        deadline = time.time() + 30
        try:
            while mac is None and time.time() < deadline:
                sock.send(probe)
                end = time.time() + 2
                while time.time() < end:
                    try:
                        pkt = sock.recv(2048)
                    except socket.timeout:
                        break
                    # ARP (reply, or gratuitous ARP) sent by the VM from the EMP IP
                    if len(pkt) >= 42 and pkt[12:14] == b"\x08\x06" \
                            and pkt[28:32] == ip and pkt[22:28] != src:
                        mac = pkt[22:28]
                        break
        finally:
            sock.close()
        if mac is None:
            self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync: no ARP reply from EMP")
            return
        mac_str = ":".join("%02x" % b for b in mac)
        res = subprocess.run(["ip", "link", "set", "dev", self.mgmt_intf, "address", mac_str],
                             capture_output=True, text=True)
        if res.returncode != 0:
            self.logger.warning("EMP MAC sync: %s", res.stderr.strip())
            return
        self.logger.info("EMP MAC %s copied to container %s", mac_str, self.mgmt_intf)
