# PR Review: add ALE OmniSwitch vAOS 8.x node support

## Summary

This PR adds a new `ale/vaos` node: a Makefile, Dockerfile, launcher (`launch.py`), and README for booting ALE OmniSwitch vAOS 8.x from a qcow2 with the GNS3 appliance's kernel/initrd/chassis-info artifacts. The launcher reuses the shared `common/vrnetlab.py` framework correctly: `_Console`'s `expect` contract is satisfied (`PROMPT_RE`, `LINK_UP_RE`, and `NOT_READY_RE` are all raw `bytes`, unlike compiled patterns which are only used with direct `re` calls), the Makefile hooks align with `makefile.include`/`makefile-sanity.include`, and the mgmt-passthrough handling (PCI re-slotting, ARP-probe MAC learning) is internally consistent with no PCI slot collisions and correct ARP field offsets.

No blocking defects were found. Three minor/optional items remain: a one-off default in `--nics` that overshoots the appliance's defined port set, stale boot-output state across VM restarts, and a missing (optional) unit test for a new pure helper.

| Priority | Title |
| --- | --- |
| P4 | `--nics` default `13` exceeds the 12 data ports defined in `PORT_MAP` |
| P4 | `self._boot_out` is never reset across VM restarts, so a stale link-up line can shortcut boot detection |
| P4 | No unit test covers the new `_extract_snapshot` helper |

## Findings

### P4 — `--nics` default `13` exceeds the 12 data ports defined in `PORT_MAP`

**Location:** [ale/vaos/docker/launch.py#L171](https://github.com/srl-labs/vrnetlab/blob/abbd9338b43ccbf8f21deebbe7ddfe40c326861a/ale/vaos/docker/launch.py#L171) and [ale/vaos/docker/launch.py#L568](https://github.com/srl-labs/vrnetlab/blob/abbd9338b43ccbf8f21deebbe7ddfe40c326861a/ale/vaos/docker/launch.py#L568)

`PORT_MAP` defines guest NIC indices 0 through 12, of which index 2 is reserved for the EMP management port — i.e. 12 data ports (`1/1/1` … `1/1/30A`, documented in `ale/vaos/README.md`). However, `--nics` defaults to `13`, so `self.num_nics = max(nics, len(PORT_MAP) - 1)` always evaluates to `13` with the default. A topology wiring 13 data interfaces produces `eth13`, which maps to guest NIC index 13 — beyond the last defined port — with no entry in `PORT_MAP` and no port name in `_log_port_map`. The comment "expose all defined ports (max)" suggests the intended ceiling is `len(PORT_MAP) - 1` = 12.

**Trigger:** A user wires 13 data links to the node, or reads the `--nics` help and passes `13` or more.

**Impact:** The last data NIC maps to a guest slot that has no corresponding appliance port; behavior there is undefined and undocumented. Minor, since the appliance only defines 13 adapters total.

**Correction:** Change the `--nics` default to `12` so it matches `len(PORT_MAP) - 1` (and update the README's interface table note if needed), keeping the `max()` guard for smaller explicit values.

### P4 — `self._boot_out` is never reset across VM restarts, so a stale link-up line can shortcut boot detection

**Location:** [ale/vaos/docker/launch.py#L253-L261](https://github.com/srl-labs/vrnetlab/blob/abbd9338b43ccbf8f21deebbe7ddfe40c326861a/ale/vaos/docker/launch.py#L253-L261)

`bootstrap_spin` accumulates console output into `self._boot_out` and never clears it. When the spin guard triggers (`spins > 6000`), `stop()` + `start()` reboot the VM, but the accumulated output from the previous boot — including a possible `+++ Link 1/1/1 operationally up` line — survives. `bootstrap_config` treats a `LINK_UP_RE` hit anywhere in `self._boot_out` as boot-complete, so after a restart it can skip waiting for the fresh boot's link-up and log in before the switch is ready.

**Trigger:** A VM that boots, prints the link-up line, but never reaches the login prompt, then goes silent for long enough to hit the spin guard and restart.

**Impact:** Low in practice: the premature login is absorbed by `_login`'s retry loop (`LOGIN_RETRIES` × `LOGIN_RETRY_DELAY` = 150 s), and `bootstrap_config`'s readiness checks (`NOT_READY_RE` with a 900 s budget) cover the rest. Still, the stale state defeats the purpose of the post-restart wait.

**Correction:** Reset the accumulator on restart — e.g. set `self._boot_out = b""` in `stop()` (or right before `self.start()` in the spin guard) so each boot's output is judged on its own.

### P4 — No unit test covers the new `_extract_snapshot` helper

**Location:** [ale/vaos/docker/launch.py#L327-L360](https://github.com/srl-labs/vrnetlab/blob/abbd9338b43ccbf8f21deebbe7ddfe40c326861a/ale/vaos/docker/launch.py#L327-L360)

`_extract_snapshot` is a pure static function with non-trivial edge cases (async console headers interleaved with config lines, the echoed command line, prompt-line detection), and it is the mechanism backing `containerlab save`. The repository already has a unit-test precedent (`fortinet/tests/`), but this PR adds no test for the new helper.

**Trigger:** Future refactors of the snapshot parser or the prompt/async regexes (e.g. `LINE_PROMPT_RE`, `ASYNC_HEADER_RE`) regress silently; `containerlab save` starts producing corrupted or truncated startup configs.

**Impact:** No automated guard on a user-visible save path; regressions would only surface at runtime.

**Correction:** Add a small pytest module under `ale/vaos/` (mirroring `fortinet/tests/`) covering: a clean snapshot, an async header line in the middle of the output, and prompt-line handling. This is optional but cheap and directly protects the changed behavior.

## Coverage**Complete:** true

Notes:
- Full source review of all four changed paths (`Makefile`, `README.md`, `Dockerfile`, `launch.py`) plus the relevant framework code in `common/vrnetlab.py` (`_Console`, `VM`, `VR`, `gen_mgmt`, `gen_nics`, `stop`/`start`/`work`) and the shared `makefile.include`/`makefile-sanity.include`.
- Verified that `PROMPT_RE` (`rb"..."`), `LINK_UP_RE`, and `NOT_READY_RE` are raw bytes and therefore compatible with `_Console.expect`'s `pat.decode()` contract; compiled `str` patterns (`LINE_PROMPT_RE`, `ASYNC_HEADER_RE`) are only used with direct `re` calls — consistent with all other launchers.
- Verified the PCI re-slotting produces no slot collisions (`eth1`→1, `eth2`→2, mgmt→3, `eth3`→4, …) and that the launcher's added dummy NICs for `eth1`/`eth2` preserve the EMP-at-guest-index-2 invariant.
- Verified the ARP probe frame layout and reply-filter byte offsets (sender MAC at 22:28, sender IP at 28:32) and the `mgmt_passthrough` handling against the patterns used by `nokia/sros` and `extreme/voss`.
- The containerlab-side `ale_vaos` kind and `containerlab save` implementation are outside this repository and could not be verified from the snapshot; the save-file handshake (`SAVE_REQUEST`/`SAVE_DONE`) is documented in `launch.py` and `README.md` but the counterpart is aspirational for older containerlab versions per the README.
- Tests were not executed (read-only source snapshot, no Docker environment); the root `README.md` supported-nodes list is explicitly partial, so omitting `ale/vaos` from it is not treated as a doc gap.
